collectionMethod: Manual capture of the official Command Code pages (English) around 10:40 Beijing time on 2026-10-28 (about 02:40Z): the public pricing page, the GOAT plan page and the pricing-limits resource page, read as published, and compared against the 2026-10-27 capture recorded in data/research/goat-shared-pool-round1-2026-10-27.json. The pricing-page GOAT/Pro credit wording (plan card, comparison table, per-plan detail blocks and the 'Which plan is right for you?' section), the plan-page FAQ heading and usage-limit block, the pricing-limits plan table and the embedded RSC payload (budgetUsd / rates / budgetSteps per model) were checked. Research-only — no adopted row generated, no adopted value changed, no script changed.
scope: Command Code GOAT official pages only. One topic changed on 2026-10-28: the public pricing page caught up with the docs pages and now advertises the GOAT plan with the same 'Up to $100' credits wording (and Pro with 'Up to $110'), so the inconsistency recorded on 2026-10-27 is gone. No per-model allowance changed (all 59 GOAT models keep the same budgetUsd / rates / budgetSteps in the embedded RSC payload), no model was added to or removed from the GOAT plan, no price changed, no leaderboard/score data touched, no OpenCode Go rows touched, no adopted.csv row.

interpretation.summary: The public pricing page caught up with the docs: as of 2026-10-28 the GOAT plan is advertised as 'Up to $100' monthly credits on the card, in the comparison table, in the GOAT detail block and in the 'Which plan is right for you?' section (Pro likewise 'Up to $110'), while the plan page and the pricing-limits page and all 59 per-model allowances stayed exactly as they were on 2026-10-27.

resolvedInconsistency.statement: The inconsistency recorded on 2026-10-27 in goat-shared-pool-round1-2026-10-27.json — the pricing page still showing a flat $70 while the docs pages already read 'Up to $100' — is eliminated. All three official pages now use the same 'up to $100' wording.
resolvedInconsistency.basis: Pricing page card, comparison table, detail block and 'Which plan is right for you?' section all changed to 'up to $100' on 2026-10-28; the plan page and pricing-limits page were already at 'up to $100' and did not move.

ambiguity.statement: The 'up to' phrasing is still ambiguous. It may only describe the maximum amount reachable under the plan (i.e. the shared pool is still $70 and a model may use up to its own allowance within it), or it may mean the shared pool cap itself is now $100. The wording change on the marketing page does not settle this.
supportingFacts: All 59 GOAT models keep their previous budgetUsd, and the highest is still Ling 3.1 Flash at $100, so no per-model allowance was raised to match a new $100 pool.
The plan page and the pricing-limits page allowances are unchanged ('up to $20' / 'up to $50' / 'up to $100'), so no allowance table moved on 2026-10-28.
The same rewrite was applied to the Pro plan ($80 -> 'Up to $110'), which suggests a marketing-wide wording change rather than a GOAT-specific pool change.

The pricing page previously carried two different flat values ($80 on the GOAT card, $70 in the comparison table), so its wording had not been a reliable source for a single pool figure in the first place.

repoPipeline.commentOnFile: Command Code GOAT: shared monthly pool $70 + per-model monthly allowance; effective=min(70, allowance).
repoPipeline.note: The pipeline still reads a flat $70 shared pool and is not changed by this capture. Under the unchanged per-model allowances, a $100 pool would only bear on models whose allowance currently exceeds $70 (Ling 3.1 Flash at $100, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (latest) at $80, GLM-5.3 Flash at $80); models at or below $70 would be unaffected. No such change is made here.
